back_translation: In those days Hezekiah became ill to the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "The LORD says this: 'Set your house in order, for you must die; you will not recover.'"
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
saying, "O LORD, remember how I have walked before You in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying:
"Go and tell Hezekiah: the LORD, the God of your father David, says this: 'I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will protect this city.
And this will be the sign to you from the LORD that the LORD will do this thing He has spoken:
"Behold, I will make the shadow cast on the stairway of Ahaz by the sun go back ten steps." So the sun went back ten steps on the stairway down which it had cast its shadow.
A composition of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been ill and recovered from his sickness:
I said: In the middle of my life I must walk through the gates of the realm of the dead; the remainder of my years has been confiscated.
I said: I will not see Yah — Yah in the land of the living; I will no longer look on mankind among the inhabitants of this world.
My dwelling has been pulled up and carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom. Day and night You bring me to my end.
I stilled myself until morning, but like a lion He breaks all my bones. Day and night You bring me to my end.
I chirp faintly like a swallow or a crane; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weary from gazing upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my guarantor.
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it. I will walk humbly and carefully all my years because of this bitterness of my soul.
O Lord, by these things people live, and the life of my spirit is in all of them. Restore me to strength and let me live.
Behold, the great bitterness I suffered turned out to be for my own welfare. In love You have drawn my life up from the pit of destruction, for You have hurled all my sins behind Your back.
For the realm of the dead cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who go down to the deep pit cannot hope in Your faithfulness.
The living, only the living can thank You, as I do today; fathers will make Your faithfulness known to their children.
The LORD will save me, and we will play my songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives at the house of the LORD.
Now Isaiah had said, "Take a cake of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover."
And Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
